Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit). Read-only investigation only — no edits.

I need to fetch ONE real, live product's full data from Salesforce Commerce Cloud (via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, this project's only sanctioned way to get commerce data — no mocking/fixtures allowed in production paths per AGENTS.md) so I can feed real values into `ZimmProductCard`'s props: `primaryImage`/`hoverImage`/`images` (each `{src: string, alt: string}`), `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` (pre-formatted display strings like `"$595.00"`), `colour`/`size` (plain strings), `name`, `href`, `badge?`, `isUnavailable?`.

Investigate and report back:

1. **Find every real usage of a commerce-sdk-react product-fetching hook in this codebase** (`grep -rn "from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react'" overrides/` and look specifically for hooks like `useProduct`, `useProducts`, `useShopperSearch`, `useSearchProducts`, `useCategory`, `useProductSearch` — whatever actually shows up, don't guess names). For each real usage found, report: the exact import, the exact call signature (what params it's given), and what shape of data comes back (read enough of the surrounding code to see which fields are actually destructured/used from the response).

2. **Look at `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/`'s own type definitions** for whichever single-product hook you find is the right one (likely `useProduct`) to get its real TypeScript return shape — specifically: where do product images live in the response (is it `imageGroups`, a flat `image` field, something else), where does price live (`price`, `prices`, a `tieredPrices` array), where do variation attributes like colour/size live (`variationAttributes`, `variationValues`), and how does the SDK represent "out of stock" (`inventory`, `c_isUnavailable`, an `orderable` boolean, something else) — report the REAL field names from the actual type definitions or from real usage in this codebase, not assumed SFCC OCAPI field names.

3. **Check whether this project has an existing SFCC product ID or slug already used anywhere** in test fixtures, Playwright specs, or documentation (`grep -rn "masterProductID\|productId" e2e/ overrides/ .docs/ 2>/dev/null | head -30`) that's confirmed to exist in a real, reachable SFCC environment (dev/test) — I'd rather reuse an already-proven-real product ID than invent one that might not exist.

4. **Check `overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts` and `use-current-customer.ts`** (both Tier 1, per `frozenFiles.md` — read-only, do not suggest modifying) just enough to confirm whether this project already has an established `CommerceApiProvider`/`QueryClientProvider` wrapping pattern at the app root (so a page-level component can just call a commerce-sdk-react hook directly without extra provider setup) — check `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` or `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` (both Tier 2) to confirm these providers are already mounted app-wide, so I know a homepage page component wouldn't need to add its own provider wrapper.

5. **Check whether a product image's real SFCC response includes usable `alt` text**, or whether callers have to synthesize their own (relevant since `ZimmProductCardMediaImage` requires a non-empty `alt` on every image) — check how `product-detail`'s own image-consuming code (if any) currently handles this.

Report as structured findings — exact hook name(s), exact field paths in the real response shape, and any already-proven-real product identifier you find. I'm using this directly to write a data-mapping function in an implementation plan, so precision on real field names beats a general description of how SFCC/OCAPI normally works.

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';

/**
 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
 *
 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
 *
 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
 *
 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
 *     leaves it visible.
 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
 *     which of the two reasons applies.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
 *
 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
 * rather than silently picked.
 *
 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
 *
 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
 */

/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;

/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];

/**
 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
 * `buildCardProps` helper.
 */
export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
  id: string;
  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
  href: string;
  name: string;
  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
  currentPrice?: string;
  originalPrice?: string;
  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
  isUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
  /**
   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
   */
  badge?: string;
};

export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
  variation: 'plp';
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
  variation: 'home';
  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
};

export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
  variation: 'wishlist';
  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
  colour: string;
  size: string;
  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
  onRemove: () => void;
  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);

type ZimmProductCardVariation =
  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];

 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
 *
 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
 *
 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
 *
 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
 *     leaves it visible.
 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
 *     which of the two reasons applies.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
 *
 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
 * rather than silently picked.
 *
 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
 *
 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
 */

/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;

/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];

/**
 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
 * `buildCardProps` helper.
 */
export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
  id: string;
  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
  href: string;
  name: string;
  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
  currentPrice?: string;
  originalPrice?: string;
  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
  isUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
  /**
   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
   */
  badge?: string;
};

export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
  variation: 'plp';
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
  variation: 'home';
  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
};

export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
  variation: 'wishlist';
  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
  colour: string;
  size: string;
  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
  onRemove: () => void;
  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);

type ZimmProductCardVariation =
  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];

Investigation complete. Findings below, organized by your five questions.

## 1. Real commerce-sdk-react product-fetching hook usages in `overrides/`

Full `grep -rn "from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react'" overrides/` result — 9 files, 3 with product-fetching hooks:

**`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:33`**
```ts
import { useProductSearch } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
...
const { data: productSearchResult, isLoading: productsLoading } = useProductSearch({
  parameters: {
    refine: [`cgid=${HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_CATEGORY_ID}`, 'htype=master'] as unknown as string,
    expand: ['promotions', 'variations', 'prices', 'images', 'custom_properties'],
    perPricebook: true,
    allVariationProperties: true,
    limit: HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_LIMIT,
  },
});
```
Only `productSearchResult?.hits` is read, and it's handed straight to `ProductScroller` (base component) unmapped — this file does **no** field-level destructuring of a hit itself.

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:38`** — the real single-product case:
```ts
import {
  useProduct,
  useProducts,
  useCategory,
  useShopperCustomersMutation,
  useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation,
  useCustomerId,
  useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper as useShopperBasketsMutationHelper,
} from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
```
Call site (line ~233):
```ts
const { data: productResponse, isLoading: isProductLoading, isError: isProductError, error: productError } = useProduct(
  {
    parameters: {
      id: requestedProductId,
      perPricebook: true,
      expand: ['availability', 'promotions', 'options', 'images', 'prices', 'variations', 'set_products', 'bundled_products', 'page_meta_tags'],
      allImages: true,
      ...(selectedInventoryId ? { inventoryIds: selectedInventoryId } : {}),
    },
  },
  { keepPreviousData: true },
);
```
`useCategory` (line 276) and `useProducts` (line 311, batch-fetching sibling variant IDs for sets/bundles) are also called. `productResponse` is then passed through the **base** hook `useProductInventory` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-product-inventory`, not commerce-sdk-react) to produce the final `product` object actually rendered — this is the real "resolved product" downstream code reads from.

Fields actually read off `product`/`productResponse` elsewhere in this file and in `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`: `imageGroups`, `master.masterId`, `variationAttributes`, `variationValues`, `type.set`/`type.bundle`, `inventory.orderable`, `primaryCategoryId`, `currency`, `id`, plus Zimmermann's own `c_*` custom attributes (see §2).

## 2. Real field shape for `useProduct` (single product)

`useProduct`'s declared type (`node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.d.ts`):
```ts
export declare const useProduct: (apiOptions, queryOptions?) => UseQueryResult<DataType<Client['getProduct']>>;
```
`DataType<Client['getProduct']>` resolves to `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `Product` type (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`, confirmed against `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`). This codebase's own docblock (product-detail/index.tsx, lines 114-127) explicitly names this as the real type and instructs importing it directly — `type SfccProduct = any;` is flagged there as **known, deliberate tech debt**, not the intended shape:
> "the shapes themselves are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s, and it does export them as `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` / `.Variant` / `.Category`... AGENTS.md's Type Definitions rule says to import those directly."
This matches AGENTS.md line 147: "Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly." `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` is present at `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/` (hoisted transitively, not a direct `package.json` dependency) and exports `ShopperProductsTypes` as a namespace. No `overrides/app/types/commerce.ts` exists yet (only `contentful.ts` and `vendor.d.ts` are in `overrides/app/types/`), so there's no pre-existing shared alias to import from within this repo — you'd import `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` from `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` directly, per that comment.

Real field paths (`Product` type, `index.esm.d.ts` ~line 32760):

| Concern | Real field path | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Images | `product.imageGroups: Array<ImageGroup>` | `ImageGroup = { images: Array<Image>; variationAttributes?: Array<VariationAttribute>; viewType: string }` |
| Image itself | `imageGroups[].images[]` | `Image = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link: string; title?: string }` |
| Price (selling) | `product.price?: number` | plain number, not a string |
| Price (other) | `product.priceRanges?: Array<{maxPrice, minPrice, pricebook}>`, `product.prices?: {[pricebookId]: number}`, `product.tieredPrices?: Array<{price, pricebook, quantity}>`, `product.priceMax`, `product.pricePerUnit` | all numbers |
| Master (list/RRP-ish) | `product.master?: { masterId: string; orderable?: boolean; price?: number; priceMax?: number; prices?: {...} }` | |
| Variation attributes | `product.variationAttributes?: Array<VariationAttribute>` where `VariationAttribute = { id: string; name?: string; values?: Array<VariationAttributeValue> }`, `VariationAttributeValue = { description?, image?: Image, imageSwatch?: Image, name?, orderable?: boolean, value: string }` | this is where colour/size names live, keyed by attribute `id` (e.g. `"color"`, `"size"`) |
| Resolved variant's own colour/size values | `product.variationValues?: { [attributeId: string]: string }` (a code, e.g. `{color: 'BLACK', size: 'M'}` — not the display name; cross-reference `variationAttributes[].values[].name` for the human-readable label) | |
| All buyable SKUs | `product.variants?: Array<Variant>`, `Variant = { orderable?, price?, productId, tieredPrices?, variationValues? }` | |
| **Stock/orderable** | `product.inventory?: Inventory` (default inventory, only present when `expand: ['availability']` is requested) — `Inventory = { ats?, backorderable?, id, inStockDate?, orderable?: boolean, preorderable?, stockLevel? }`. Also `Variant.orderable`, `Master.orderable`. | **There is no `c_isUnavailable` field anywhere in the SDK type.** The real signal is `inventory.orderable` (boolean) — confirmed by actual usage in `product-view/index.tsx:290`: `(variant?.orderable \|\| product?.inventory?.orderable) && quantity > 0 && quantity <= stockLevel`. `ZimmProductCard`'s `isUnavailable?: boolean` is this project's own presentational inversion of that, not a literal passthrough SFCC field. |
